incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 502/timeout rate for MyriadCorp (vpc-0a1b2c) — Private deployment (eu-west-1). Affected path: inference.myriadcorp.internal -> dedicated pool myr-dedicated-3. Error rate: 18% (1m), 9% (5m). Paging @alexa_oncall
alexa_oncall: On it. Pulling logs + target health. Any recent infra/sg/dns changes?
matt_sre: Not from SRE side in the last 24h. I'll check NLB target health and conntrack metrics.
priya_netops: There was an automated security-group egress hardening rolled last night for customer VPCs as part of lockdown ticket 7832. Checking diffs now.
sam_se: Customer reports app-level retries spiking, timeouts after prefix-cache misses. They also see intermittent DNS NXDOMAIN for internal names.
ivy_platform: Console shows NLB target group 3/6 healthy -> 1/6 healthy. ALB in front returning 502s. Hosts' /health returns 200 locally.
alexa_oncall: If hosts pass local health but NLB shows failing, could be outbound/connectivity from node -> health probe address or conntrack. Any DNS TTL changes?
priya_netops: No DNS config changes in our control plane. Audit shows SG change: sg-lockdown-2026-03-15 applied to customer security groups (egress tightened). Change ID sg-aurora-20260315.
matt_sre: Tcpdump on node during probe shows probe SYN arriving, node sends RST. /proc/sys/net/nf_conntrack_count high -> conntrack table near full. Suspect NAT/conntrack exhaustion leading to resets.
sam_se: Customer NAT instances metrics show conntrack count spiking after a small canary service rollout. They may be leaking connections.
alexa_oncall: Quick mitigation options: 1) open temporary egress from dedicated pool nodes to customer subnets + NLB health IP ranges, 2) bump conntrack size, or 3) shift traffic to another healthy dedicated pool. Which is fastest?
priya_netops: Easiest immediate action is temp SG permit for outbound 80/443 to customer subnets + NLB probe IPs. I'll prepare a narrow rule and tag it temporary.
deploy-bot: Request to apply change: sg-allow-temp-egress-51321 queued.
priya_netops: Applying rule now: +egress tcp 80,443 -> 10.0.0.0/21 (customer subnets) ; +egress tcp 1024:65535 -> 10.0.6.0/24 (NLB health range). Patch id sg-allow-temporary-egress-51321.
deploy-bot: Change applied: sg-allow-temporary-egress-51321 at 2026-03-17T08:26:12Z by priya_netops. Audit ref a-51321.
matt_sre: Conntrack counts dropping after rule apply; NLB health checks showing 5/6 healthy now. Starting gradual traffic shift back to myr-dedicated-3.
sam_se: Customer confirms 502s reduced — errors down from 18% -> 2% in the last 5m. They are still seeing occasional spikes when cache cold.
ivy_platform: Note: need long-term fix — either increase conntrack or introduce NAT pooling / reserved egress for customer's dedicated pool. Will open PI/bug.
alexa_oncall: Creating follow-up incident ticket and runbook entry. Temp SG rule will be reverted after 30m if stable; will coordinate revert with customer and netops.
priya_netops: Scheduling revert job for 09:00 UTC unless we get a regression. Capturing config diff and change rationale.
sam_se: Customer asked for recommended architecture: suggest reserved NAT gateway + connection pooling, and egress monitoring. I'll draft a migration plan.
matt_sre: Marking immediate incident mitigated. Keeping 1h watch window. If error rate >5% re-paging.
alexa_oncall: Handoff to @ivy_platform for 1h monitoring and post-incident writeup. If regressions, escalate to infra oncall. :thumbsup:
ivy_platform: Watching metrics; no regression seen in last 20m. Will collect logs and produce summary. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED: INCIDENT STATUS -> Mitigated. Summary saved to incident-5132109876. Reminder: revert temp change or approve permanent egress exception.
